The change

This example explains BitPlan's live annotation flow. The document and its notes are separate, so a reviewer can comment without replacing the plan.

Example note · not shared

“Can a second reader see this note after reloading?”

How it works

01Add a note

Choose a place in the document and write your comment.

02Encrypt

The browser encrypts the contribution before sending it.

03Synchronize

Convex sends the saved change to connected readers.

04Read together

Their browsers decrypt and display the annotation.

Ask your agent:
Read the current plan and its annotations.
Explain what you would change, and which notes led to it.
Keep unresolved feedback in the next draft.

Test it

  1. Open the collaboration invitation in two sessions.
  2. Save a text note in one session.
  3. Check the other session, then reload it.
  4. Confirm the note is still attached to the right passage.

Share deliberately

A complete reader link is a key to the plan. Send it privately, and keep it out of public chats, screenshots, and repositories. A collaboration invitation also lets its holder contribute.

For sensitive work, ask your agent to create a wallet-encrypted plan for named contacts without a reader link.

Manage contacts with your agent

Ask: “Verify Dave's public identity key with me, save him as a contact, and create a new hosted plan encrypted to Dave and my wallet. Do not create a reader link.”

npx bitplan contact set dave <verified-public-identity-key>
npx bitplan contact list
npx bitplan upload ./private-plan.html --hosted --share-with dave

Use a new plan file for this example. Existing drafts can retain earlier reader-link recipients; leaving off --link does not revoke them. Contacts are local labels. Never give your agent a private key or wallet password.

Reading permission is separate from the live collaboration invitation. Removing a recipient affects future versions, not copies already shared.

How to use this plan

Open a collaboration invitation to join. Right-click beside a passage and choose + T to add a note. Enter saves it; Shift+Enter adds a line. If your browser takes over right-click, use the Annotations button.

For images, choose Photos, Stickers, or Draw. Notes belong to the annotation layer; they do not rewrite the document. Read them before publishing your next revision.

A hosted revision is not an on-chain record. Annotation checkpoints on chain are still planned.
